content:
maria: Heads-up — saw a steady memory/residency climb in the KV reservoir during long-context cont-batch runs. After ~35s we start getting HOL blocking on merged batches, tail latency spikes.
maria: Repro steps: run the perf harness with long ctx and enabled cont-batch merge: `./tools/run_longctx_kv_harness --clients 8 --seq 16000 --merge-interval 10ms`
raj: repro useful, thanks. Is this only on the new kernel-selection tweak we rolled Friday? Any regression windows?
maria: It correlates with the kernel change (2026-03-12) that altered the small-kernel fallback. Before that the sweep pass reclaimed more small fragments.
oliver: My quick read: the change reduced aggressive small-kernel coalescing, so we might be leaving more tiny KV fragments. When cont-batch tries to merge, it hits many fragmented slots -> more allocations and HOL waits.
sasha: I toggled `contbatch.smart_merge=false` in staging yesterday — CPU went down but short-ctx p50 got slightly worse. Might be tradeoff between merge work and fragmentation overhead.
ben: Can we see the runtime log lines around the spike? Even a couple of samples would help.
maria: pasted a condensed log sample below (from one run):
```
[KV] t=00:00:36 reserve_mb=1452 resident_mb=1536 fragments=112 merge_attempts=28 hol_wait_ms=240
[KV] t=00:00:38 sweep_passes=3 reclaimed_mb=4 contbatch_pending=6 alloc_failures=2
[RT] tail_latency_ms p99=1123 p95=410 p50=75
```
raj: fragments=112 and low reclaimed_mb is suspicious. Sweep_passes=3 but reclaim tiny amount.
oliver: Agree. Two hypotheses: (1) kernel-selection change produces many sub-allocs with incompatible alignment so sweep can't coalesce them; (2) merge heuristic triggers head-of-line because it waits for large contiguous KV slots.
sasha: We should add a metric for "kv_fragment_size_hist" and a counter for "merge_blocked_by_hol". Quick dashboard would show if merges are waiting for contiguous runs vs waiting for async reclaim.
ben: I can add a short-lived probe to staging to emit histogram and a boolean when merge waits >50ms. Want me to push? @maria
maria: please, that would help. Also can we enable a targeted GC pass after merge failures to see immediate effects?
oliver: I can prep a patch that tweaks sweep aggression when fragments > 64 and contbatch_pending > 4 (safe default). We should gate behind a runtime flag: `kv.sweep_aggressive=true`.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary staging with flag `kv.sweep_aggressive=true` tomorrow 02:00 UTC — link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/ops/7890
raj: If the aggressive sweep reduces fragments and hol_wait_ms, we can consider reverting the kernel fallback or adding a small-kernel coalesce path.
sasha: Also worth profiling the merge path flamegraph to see hot alloc/free sites. Maria, can you attach one?
maria: Uploaded flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/abcd123 — main hot leaf is `kv::alloc_fragment` called from `contbatch::try_merge_batches`.
ben: Good find. If alloc_fragment is hot, then forced coalesce or pre-reserve contiguous block might avoid churn.
oliver: Plan: (1) add fragment histogram + merge-blocked metric (ben) (2) land `kv.sweep_aggressive` flag in staging (oliver) (3) run cont-batch harness with flag on/off and compare flamegraphs/p95/p99 (maria/sasha). I'll open a PR for the sweep tweak.
raj: Sounds good. If we see immediate improvement, we should target a quick patch release. Otherwise continue kernel-fallback investigation.
maria: Thanks all — will run another controlled experiment once the staging probe is up and report numbers here. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Canary completed: staging run with `kv.sweep_aggressive=true` finished (id: 2026-03-15T02:45Z). Summary: fragments down ~45%, hol_wait_ms median down from 210->60ms, p99 latency improved ~18%.
maria: Nice, prelim numbers look promising. I'll re-run the 8-client longctx harness and upload new flamegraph later today.
